appraisal_events.evidence: Cette marque flagrante d'ignorance lui fit froncer le sourcil... il vint rudement me tirer... une place dans l'autre salle... le patron m'en refusa une autre en me disant : « Non, monsieur, je ne peux pas gêner tout le monde pour vous. »
appraisal_events.explanation: The restaurant patron, initially welcoming, turns visibly contemptuous once the narrator fumbles with the revolving door, then roughly ejects him from the aristocratic room and coldly refuses him a better seat elsewhere.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Alors ça te fait plaisir de te marier, Bibi ? » ne pouvait s'empêcher de s'exclamer le prince de Châtellerault, qui laissait tomber sa fourchette d'étonnement et de désespoir... Dieu sait tout ce que son père avait adroitement conté aux Ambresac contre la mère de Bibi... il songeait qu'il fallait au plus vite faire volte-face en direction de Mlle de la Canourque ou de Miss Foster.
appraisal_events.explanation: Châtellerault's visible shock and despair at Bibi's engagement announcement exposes his own thwarted, secretly schemed pursuit of the same match (including his father's slander of Bibi's mother), and he is immediately shown scrambling for a fallback bride while Bibi answers with composed grace.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator is pulled out of the reserved aristocratic room and denied any better seat, marking him as locally out of place and unwelcome.
He is exposed as envious and hypocritical, having covertly worked against a match he publicly praised.
He visibly loses composure (dropping his fork in shock and despair) and must scramble to save face with a backup plan.
Bibi comes out comparatively ahead: he secures the desired match and answers Châtellerault's jealous probing with poised, unruffled charm.

ambiguities: "Bibi" is a nickname whose full identity is not otherwise established in the passage or reference sheet; it is treated as a distinct named figure from the prince de Châtellerault who addresses him.
